name: Ellbögen
kurzbeschreibung: High-altitude scattered settlement in the Stubaital, featuring traditional farming and sweeping views over the Wipptal.
title: Ellbögen
metaDescription: Ellbögen in the Wipptal valley at the foot of Patscherkofel: Scenic mountain farming village, historic Hinterlocher Mill, Arztal hikes and alpine panoramas.
text:
Overview

Ellbögen is situated at an altitude of 1,070 meters on a sun-drenched terrace of the eastern low mountain range in the Wipptal valley, located southeast of Innsbruck in the district of Innsbruck-Land. Home to approximately 1,150 residents, this peaceful municipality comprises traditional hamlets including Saint Peter, Erlach, Oberellbögen, and Innerellbögen. Topographically, the municipal boundary extends from the gorges of the Sill river up to the summit of Mount Rosenjoch (2,796 m) in the Tux Alps. Shielded along the eastern slopes of Mount Patscherkofel, Ellbögen captivates visitors with tranquility far from transit corridors and commanding vistas overlooking Mount Serles, the Stubai Alps, and the Nordkette.

History

Settlement of the fertile plateau dates back to Roman antiquity; the village was first documented in 1032, appearing in monastic registers around 1170 as Ellenbogen. The name reflects the topographical curve of the Wipptal valley, which bends like an elbow at this point. For centuries, the historic Lower Roman Road ran through Ellbögen, developing in the Middle Ages into a vital salt highway carrying salt from the royal mines at Hall in Tirol south towards Italy. The area gained industrial significance through mining in the Arztal valley (historically Erzthal or Ore Valley), where copper and iron were extracted during the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, utilized among other works for casting the famous Black Men bronze figures at Innsbruck's Imperial Court Church. A remarkable historic landmark is the Hinterlocher Mill along the Falkasanerbach brook, featuring a drive wheel carved with the date 1738 and operating today as an authentic working museum mill. The Late Gothic parish church of Saints Peter and Paul was constructed in 1472 by master builder Stefan von Matrei.

Getting There

By automobile from Innsbruck, Ellbögen is reached in just fifteen minutes via the Brenner motorway A13, exiting at Patsch/Europabrücke and following regional road L38. Traveling from the south, motorists exit the A13 at Matrei am Brenner. Alternatively, the toll-free federal road B182 runs through the lower Wipptal to Schönberg, connecting directly with the L38. Rail travelers arrive at Innsbruck Central Station or take S-Bahn line S3 to Matrei am Brenner railway station. From Innsbruck main station, VVT regional bus line 560 provides frequent daily service via Patsch, serving all hamlets of Ellbögen. Overnight guests travel free on regional public transport holding the Wipptal guest card.

Tips

A classic alpine hike starts in Oberellbögen, passing the historic Hinterlocher Mill through pine forests into the quiet Arztal valley to the rustic Arztaler Alm at 1,900 meters, where heritage Tyrolean livestock breeds graze peacefully. In the adjacent Viggartal valley, the historic Meißner Haus alpine refuge provides traditional refreshments. Experienced mountaineers can summit the Kreuzspitze or Rosenjoch for sweeping panoramic vistas over the Central Alps. Nature lovers can easily access the celebrated Zirbenweg panoramic trail on Mount Patscherkofel, weaving through one of the oldest Swiss stone pine forests in Europe. A relaxed walk along the historical salt route showcases beautifully preserved Tyrolean wooden farmsteads.
